evals.prompt: Line edit this scene from my novel: evals/files/01-farmhouse.md. Notes in chat, please.
evals.expected_output: Finds seven planted craft problems of different kinds, each with an effect and a cause, and routes the two typos to the summary.
expectations: The summary states a voice baseline covering at least two of: sentence shape, register, psychic distance, tense, period
Flags the ambiguous pronoun in "Ruth told her sister she had left the back gate open"
Flags the blocking problem in "With the lamp held in both hands, she turned the key"
Flags "Climbing the stairs, the smell grew stronger" as a dangling modifier
Flags "Fear was a cold hand at her throat, and she swallowed it down" as a mixed figure
Flags "process" in "She needed a minute to process it" as out of period or register
Flags "You know Daddy's been dead three years this March" as characters telling each other what both already know
Flags the echo of "blister" across "begun to blister" and "A blister of damp"
Lists "off off" and "form" as mechanical errors in the summary rather than as separate line notes
Labels every note as Likely issue, Continuity, Taste, or Protect
Every Likely issue note names a cause, not only an impression
Every note quotes the manuscript text exactly, without paraphrase or silent correction
No note supplies replacement words, phrases, or sentences

evals.prompt: Can you line edit evals/files/02-flood.md? Just reply in chat.
evals.expected_output: Treats the narrator's dialect, refrain, fragments, and cumulative sentences as style, while still catching a POV slip and a tense slip.
expectations: The voice baseline names at least two of the passage's deliberate devices: the refrain, fragments, anaphora, the long cumulative sentence, or dialect
Does not flag the refrain "The water was coming up" as a Likely issue
Does not flag the fragments "Beans first." or "Brown water. Cold." as Likely issues
Does not flag the "I thought about" anaphora or the long "and how" sentence as Likely issues
Does not flag the cumulative "which was a good fence, which was the best fence on Cold Creek Road, and which went under like it never was" as a Likely issue
Does not flag "would of", "ain't", or "Get them shoes on" as errors, including in any mechanical-errors list
Flags "He was thinking he ought to have sold her in March" as knowledge the narrator can't have from the porch
Flags "Pa is leading" as a tense slip
Every note quotes the manuscript text exactly, without paraphrase or silent correction
No note supplies replacement words, phrases, or sentences

evals.prompt: Line edit evals/files/03-letter.md. Chat is fine.
evals.expected_output: A clean passage. The edit stays short, invents no problems, and grounds any Protect notes in a cause.
expectations: The summary states a voice baseline
Contains at most one Likely issue note
Does not flag the parallel "It was addressed to him. It was dated" or the "and ... and" final sentence as Likely issues
Every Protect note names the cause of the effect it protects
Every note quotes the manuscript text exactly, without paraphrase or silent correction
Contains no generic praise or notes without a named cause

evals.prompt: Line edit evals/files/04-saltmarsh.md. My style sheet is evals/files/04-saltmarsh-style-sheet.md. Notes in chat.
evals.expected_output: Respects every style-sheet decision, flags the one line that breaks the sheet, and still catches a local craft problem.
expectations: Does not flag the spelling "grey"
Does not flag "tidewife" or "drownfolk" for italics, capitalization, or a missing gloss
Does not flag the dropped g's in Del's lines "pickin'" or "Nothin'"
Does not flag the present tense
Flags Tessa's "I'm comin' back" as conflicting with the style sheet, which reserves dropped g's for Del
Flags "like a mirror, like a knife blade, like the skin on warm milk" as stacked or competing figures
Every note quotes the manuscript text exactly, without paraphrase or silent correction
No note supplies replacement words, phrases, or sentences

evals.prompt: Line edit evals/files/05-visit.md, the scene where Marisol gets her brother to sign.
evals.expected_output: With no delivery instruction and a local Markdown file that can't take comments, returns identified notes in chat and leaves the file untouched. Notes one or two instances of a recurring phrase and lists the rest, and sends the off-page turn of the scene to a developmental pass in a line.
expectations: Returns the notes in chat rather than writing them to the manuscript or to another file
Does not claim the notes were posted as comments, since a local Markdown file has no comment support
Leaves 05-visit.md unchanged, with no notes, comments, or markers inserted into the prose
Every note starts with a bold **[Line]** identifier followed by its label
Comments on no more than two instances of "for a moment"
The summary names "for a moment" as a recurring pattern and lists the locations of the instances not commented on
Flags "he signed only after she told him about the second mortgage" for a developmental pass, because the scene turns off-page on information the passage never set up
Keeps that concern to a sentence or two, with no restructuring plan, scene outline, or editorial letter
Every note quotes the manuscript text exactly, without paraphrase or silent correction
No note supplies replacement words, phrases, or sentences

evals.prompt: Line edit evals/files/06-saint-agnes.md. Notes in chat.
evals.expected_output: Builds a separate voice baseline for each narrator and judges each section against its own: Ivy's fragments and "like" are style, but a past-tense verb in her present-tense section is a slip, and Walter's borrowed quotative "like" breaks his formal register.
expectations: States a separate voice baseline for Ivy and for Walter, not one baseline for the whole passage
Ivy's baseline names at least two of: present tense, fragments, "like" as comparison or quotative, teen idiom such as "I literally cannot"
Walter's baseline names at least two of: past tense, long multi-clause sentences, formal diction, no contractions in narration
Does not flag Ivy's fragments, her "like" constructions, or "I literally cannot" as Likely issues or mechanical errors
Does not flag Walter's long sentences or formal diction as stiff, wordy, or overwritten
Flags "Grandpa stuck his to his coat" as a tense slip in Ivy's present-tense section
Flags "he was like, she's resting, go on in" as outside Walter's register
Every note starts with a bold **[Line]** identifier followed by its label
Every note quotes the manuscript text exactly, without paraphrase or silent correction
No note supplies replacement words, phrases, or sentences

evals.prompt: Line edit evals/files/07-funeral.md, from one of Mara's chapters. The style sheet is evals/files/07-funeral-style-sheet.md. Notes in chat.
evals.expected_output: Respects the no-commas decision throughout, but keeps one note as Taste where that decision creates a garden-path sentence that stops the run the decision is meant to produce, and cites the decision.
expectations: Does not flag the missing commas in narration, or the long comma-free sentences in general, as Likely issues or mechanical errors
Does not flag the comma in Mama's line "Breathe, baby." as breaking the style sheet
Keeps a note on "When they lifted the casket tipped" explaining that the reader takes "the casket" as the object of "lifted" and has to reread
Labels that note Taste, not Likely issue
That note cites the style sheet's decision that narration uses no commas
Every note starts with a bold **[Line]** identifier followed by its label
Every note quotes the manuscript text exactly, without paraphrase or silent correction
No note supplies replacement words, phrases, or sentences
